evals.prompt: I just came back from a discovery call with GlobalRetail Inc. Notes: Currently on Prometheus + Grafana + ELK, evaluating Datadog vs New Relic. Three challenges: (1) no unified observability across their AWS EKS clusters in us-east-1 and a fleet of legacy VMs, (2) no distributed tracing for their checkout and payment microservices, (3) slow incident response due to fragmented logs across tools. Use cases: APM for the checkout flow, Kubernetes monitoring via Cluster Agent, centralized log management for the VM fleet. Target state: full Datadog stack replacing Prometheus/Grafana/ELK. Competitor in eval: New Relic. Expected ROI: reduce MTTR by 40%. Presenter: Jane Doe. Customer contact: John Smith, VP Engineering. Meeting date: 2026-08-20. Include the reference resources slide. Need an architecture diagram for the Kubernetes monitoring use case slide. Output file: globalretail_demo.pptx. Build me the demo deck.
evals.expected_output: A slide plan and (tooling permitting) a finished pptx following the standard flow, AND (only for the version with Step 6) a mandatory final invocation of creating-architecture-via-excalidraw using the same original notes as-is, producing an architecture blueprint/diagram for the EKS + VM + checkout microservices environment. Slide 2 is the six-part agenda titled 'Agenda for GlobalRetail Inc.' (Intro & Whiteboard, Observe, Act, Secure, Why Datadog, Next Steps & Close) built with build_agenda.py. The notes have no customer quotes, so the third column header reads FROM MY NOTES. Because none of the three use cases is a security use case, the skill should ask how to map them to Observe, Act and Secure rather than silently renaming parts. The deck follows the 26-slide flow with a benefits tracker (Part, Use Case, Benefits to GlobalRetail, What Demonstrates It) after each of the six parts; benefits come from the notes (for example the 40% MTTR target) and no other figures are invented. All slide text is concise (fragments, rule of 3, within the writing-style.md word limits) and check_wording.py passes on the finished deck.

evals.prompt: Discovery notes for Bitsburg Bank. Head of Platform said: "We have the data. We do not have the answers. Someone still has to go and look." Call center hears about failed bill payments before engineering does; they also run an LLM fraud agent and want to know if it is healthy and what it costs. SRE lead: "Half of our incident time is spent proving that the network or legacy core did not cause the problem." and "Who approved an action, what evidence supported it, and whether it worked." CTO: "The hard part is determining which one is real before an attacker or a customer feels the impact." Concerns: do not want yet another tool, can we trust AI with bank data, cannot instrument every acquired environment in two weeks. VP Eng and CTO asking whether this is a platform worth standardizing on. 6 success criteria agreed. Use cases: (1) see failing bill payments before customers call with Journey Monitoring, RUM, APM, LLM Observability; (2) restore failed bill payments faster under governance with Bits AI SRE, approval and audit trail; (3) protect customers from account compromise with Cloud SIEM and Bits AI Security Analyst. Next step: PoC plus QVA. Show the benefits to Bitsburg as I go through the demo. Presenter: me. Output: bitsburg_demo.pptx. Build the demo deck.
evals.expected_output: Slide 2 is the agenda titled 'Agenda for Bitsburg Bank' with exactly six rows in order: Intro & Whiteboard, Observe (Use Case 1: see failing bill payments before customers call), Act (Use Case 2: restore failed bill payments faster, under governance), Secure (Use Case 3: protect customers from account compromise), Why Datadog, Next Steps & Close. The third column header reads CUSTOMER QUESTION; verbatim quotes are in curly quotes with role attribution (Head of Platform, CTO) and concerns without verbatim wording are italic questions. No quotes are invented. What Demonstrates It lists 6 success criteria, the products per use case, and PoC + QVA. The rendered agenda fits above the Datadog footer logo. Six benefits trackers (slides 6, 9, 12, 15, 21, 24) repeat the table with a BENEFITS TO BITSBURG column: parts already covered show their benefits, the part just covered is highlighted, later parts are dimmed, and the last tracker has every row filled in. The rest of the deck follows the 26-slide flow, and the skill finishes by invoking creating-architecture-via-excalidraw. All slide text is concise (fragments, rule of 3, within the writing-style.md word limits) and check_wording.py passes on the finished deck.
